tool.title: Francis Halzen
tool.excerpt: == Books == With Alan Martin he co-authored Quarks and Leptons: An Introductory Course in Modern Particle Physics (1984), a standard textbook in particle physics. == Awards == 1994: Fellow of the American Physical Society 2013: Breakthrough of the Year Award by the journal Physics World for the first-time discovery of cosmic neutrinos beyond the Milky Way 2015: Balzan Prize 2015: Giuseppe and Vanna Cocconi Prize of the European Physical Society 2018: Bruno Pontecorvo Prize for significant contribution to the IceCube detector construction and experimental discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. 2019: Yodh Prize of IUPAP 2021: Homi Bhabha Medal and Prize of IUPAP and TIFR 2024 Elected to National Academy of Sciences 2026: APS Medal for Exceptional Achievement in Research 2026: Nobel Prize in Physics "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin” == Personal life == Halzen is Belgian but also has United States citizenship. == References == == External links == Francis Halzen on Nobelprize.org Halzen, Francis (6 April 2021). "IceCube: the discovery of cosmic neutrinos" (PDF). ... Francis Louis Halzen (born 23 March 1944) is a Belgian-American particle physicist and Nobel laureate. As of October 2026 he is the Vilas Research Professor and Gregory Breit Professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and also the principal investigator of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station in Antarctica, the world's largest neutrino detector. In 2026, Halzen was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin." == Early life and ed

(created with AI) - Image by © CiberCuba Spain has officially released two new royal decrees on housing, directly impacting tenants, landlords, and prospective first-time homebuyers. These were approved by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez on October 6 and subsequently published in the Official State Gazette (BOE) on October 7. The first, Royal Decree-Law 29/2026, offers a comprehensive package of housing measures, while Royal Decree-Law 28/2026 focuses on the duration and renewal of standard residential lease agreements. Decrees Amidst Political Transition These decrees emerge after previous housing bills were rejected by parliament. The current scenario differs significantly as both the Congress of Deputies and the Senate are dissolved ahead of the general elections scheduled for November 29. Normally, the Congress of Deputies would vote on these decrees. However, with the dissolution of the legislative bodies on October 6, the Permanent Deputation of Congress now holds the authority to address these legislative texts until a new Congress is formed. Key Dates and Implementation Royal Decree-Law 29/2026 takes effect on October 8, 2026, just a day after its publication, with some provisions having their own timelines. This means that certain measures will start applying immediately without waiting for ratification by the Permanent Deputation. If the Permanent Deputation ratifies it, the decree remains in force; if not, it will be nullified instantly. Significant Housing Reforms Among the impactful changes for tenants is the reinstatement of an extraordinary lease extension of up to two years for select residential contracts. This allows tenants to request annual renewals, up to a total of two additional years, for contracts ending before December 31, 2028. Conditions include the tenant’s consistent rent payment for the past eight months. Regarding rent increases, the decree imposes a special cap on annual rent adjustments until December 31, 2027.
